subject: Pricing fidelity request — written assurance & fallback schedule
messages:

Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing fidelity and fallback options for Cloudora evaluation

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looks promising. We are running a short bake (6 weeks) to compare Redwood against AltServe for our inference tier. Procurement has two asks we need in writing before we can proceed to procurement approval:

1) A written price-fidelity assurance for 12 months that prevents a unilateral price increase above X% without 60 days notice (this is a procurement requirement).
2) A clear, documented fallback schedule/plan if runtime parity or availability degrades (we need a technical and commercial fallback so our SREs and Finance can evaluate risk).

Could you confirm whether Redwood can provide a price-assurance letter and a short commercial fallback schedule (including any migration credits or guaranteed transit credits)? Attached is our RFP summary (high level).

Attachments: Cloudora_RFP_Q2.pdf (pdf, 240KB)

Appreciate a short written response we can show legal/procurement. If helpful, Karthik from your side can join a 30-min call.

—Sarah
Sarah Lewis
Head of Platform Engineering, Cloudora
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@cloudora.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing fidelity and fallback options for Cloudora evaluation

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the RFP.

Short answer: yes, we can provide a written price-fidelity commitment and a commercial fallback schedule, with a few caveats that I summarize below so your procurement and legal teams have context.

Price-fidelity letter (what we can commit to):
- We can offer a 12-month price protection that caps any per-token increase to 7% year-over-year for the contracted SKUs under this deal (hosted API + Dedicated pool).
- Exceptions: changes in cloud provider egress fees or new regulatory taxes may be passed through with 30 days notice (we will enumerate these in the formal letter).

Fallback schedule (commercial + ops):
- Canary fallback: automatic routing to a validated smaller model variant (cost-optimized) if latencies exceed SLA by >20% for >5 minutes.
- Migration credit: 12 weeks of a migration credit equal to 25% of committed monthly spend, applied to onboarding if you sign a Dedicated contract within 60 days of notifying us of a migration due to performance issues.
- Performance rebate: if average token-latency exceeds SLA for a billing month, we provide a proportional rebate up to 10% of that month's invoice for the affected route.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik will draft the commercial assurances + fallback schedule (short, 1–2 pages) for your procurement/legal to review.
2) We schedule a 30-min alignment call with your SRE and our runtime team (Marissa suggested she join for the ops checklist).
3) If acceptable, legal can take the 1–2 page assurance as an exhibit to the MSA.

Can you share a couple of time slots (Monday/Tuesday next week) for the call? I’ll ask Karthik to circulate the draft by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priya — procurement here. Couple clarifying items before we lock in times:

1) The price-fidelity cap you propose (7%) is in the right direction. We need a line item that says Redwood will not increase unit price for the contracted SKUs for 12 months except for the limited external pass-through items you called out.
2) For the migration credit: procurement wants the mechanics spelled out (how credit applies, timing, any pro-rated calculations).

I’m attaching our standard PO and a short procurement questionnaire (Procurement_Qs.xlsx). If you can provide a 1–2 page assurance that addresses the two points above and the mechanics of the migration credit, legal can do an initial read and let you know if they need MSA-level redlines.

Hi Daniel / Sarah — Karthik here (runtime & commercial ops). Quick operational mechanics to include in the 1–2 page assurance:

Migration credit mechanics (proposal):
- Trigger: Cloudora issues formal notice citing sustained SLA degradation (>=20% breach over 72 hours) and elects migration assistance.
- Credit calculation: credit = min(25% of average monthly committed spend, actual documented migration costs up to the credit cap). We will require simple supporting invoices from Cloudora for migration expenses (standard procurement practice).
- Application: credit applied to monthly invoices starting the first full billing cycle after migration begins; unused credit expires after 12 months.

Fallback technical fallthroughs (ops):
- Automatic routing to quantized model variants within the same model family when latency degrades; we’ll provide a checklist of supported model variants and expected quality delta.
- Emergency region failover: if a region is degraded, requests can be re-routed to a secondary region with documented expected latency delta; we will include the runbook as an appendix.

Commercial guardrails:
- The price-fidelity letter will state the 7% cap and explicitly list pass-through exceptions (cloud egress, regulatory taxes).
- We recommend a canary pilot (2 weeks) under the final agreement to validate routing and KV-cache behavior; during the pilot Redwood will commit a 50% onboarding discount for the first month of pilot run (applied after invoice).

I’ll draft the assurance and the technical appendix. Priya — I’ll loop legal on the draft for exhibit language.

—Karthik
Director, Runtime & Ops, Redwood Inference
